For the Emmanuel, being truly dead, is placed in a tomb. But he lived again, as I said a little while ago. Through his death in the flesh, he confirms that he became flesh, although he is God, the Word. And through his trampling of death, he clearly shows that he is God by nature. What do they deprive human nature of, the goods that come from resurrection, and why do they slander the end of the economy of the flesh? pass_b_english: Christ's death and resurrection are the foundation of our faith, and it is through these events that we are freed from the bonds of sin and death, running beyond the bonds of death to attain a state better than sin.

The gospel, which was delivered to us by the apostles, is the message of salvation that has been revealed to us through the revelation of Jesus Christ, and it is not something that came into mind simply and without torture, but rather it is the gospel that the apostle received, with the knowledge of the one who became human for us, as he himself said, 'Not even I received it from man, nor was I taught, but through the revelation of Jesus Christ' (Galatians 1:12).

If the one delivering the gospel is taught by God, how can it not be true what is preached through him, that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, clearly of both the old and new testaments?
Many have borne witness to Christ's death and resurrection.

Through his death and resurrection, Christ has removed the sin of the world and given us the gift of eternal life, and it is necessary to say not only that he died, but also that he was buried, for the Emmanuel, being truly dead, is placed in a tomb.

But he lived again, as I said a little while ago, and through his death in the flesh, he confirms that he became flesh, although he is God, the Word, and through his trampling of death, he clearly shows that he is God by nature, and the Word from God the Father is not foreign to giving life to the temple, but rather it is his own body, through which he is said to have died for us, so that the good of resurrection might truly be found for us.

For the whole human nature was in him trampling death; thus we are said to be buried and risen with him, to sit and be in heavenly places, and he is said to have risen according to the scriptures, to have appeared to the holy apostles, and to some in part and in multitude, and he appeared to me also as to one of the lowliest of the apostles.

The church is being persecuted and strengthened, except that we have been pitied and called by Christ to apostleship, and the great mystery of the resurrection is not unknown to the ancient saints, for it has been revealed to them, and if Christ is preached as risen from the dead, how can some among you claim that there is no resurrection of the dead?

It is astonishing that some are persuaded otherwise, contrary to the sacred and divine scriptures, and dare to think differently, for if Christ died not to remain dead, but to be found stronger than death and corruption, and to become a way and door for human nature to be able to overcome corruption and return to life, then it is puzzling that the bonds of death still hold sway over those for whom God is said to have died and been raised according to his nature, being Emmanuel.

What is being denied to human nature, the benefits that come from resurrection, and why is the culmination of the flesh's economy being slandered, for if Christ has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep and the firstborn from the dead, then it is only logical that the rest will follow the firstfruits, and will be in company with the firstborn, as is fitting for the firstborn, and the apostle Paul himself testifies to this, saying...
When Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, it is equivalent to saying that he has been raised from the dead (1 Corinthians 15:12).
